name: Data Pipelines Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday data pipelines work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical data pipelines tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday data pipelines work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical data pipelines tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Prefer explicit, readable data pipelines solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
2. Validate data pipelines outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
3. Keep data pipelines changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Prefer the simplest data pipelines approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
5. Document any non-obvious data pipelines decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
6. When data pipelines guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
7. When data pipelines decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
8. Re-check edge cases relevant to data pipelines (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
9. Surface known limitations of a chosen data pipelines approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated data pipelines concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop data pipelines edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid introducing new data pipelines abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for data pipelines, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
